added_models.model: Cynomolgus monkey and CD-1 mouse oral PK/PD (presystemic ISG induction)

engagement.population: Unselected (HBeAg-positive or -negative CHB, viremic or NA-suppressed)
engagement.note: Oral GS-9620 in cynomolgus monkeys and CD-1 mice induced blood OAS1/MX1 ISGs at doses without detectable serum IFN-α.
engagement.quote: It is noteworthy that we also demonstrated that, in animals and healthy human volunteers, oral administration of GS-9620 can induce a type I interferon-dependent antiviral innate immune response, as measured by whole-blood mRNA of the ISGs
engagement.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: monkey and mouse oral PK/PD defining the presystemic window preceded the unregistered healthy-volunteer study (Lopatin 2013); paper epub 2013-10-16. Abstract-level reading (full text not retrieved).

engagement.magnitude_basis: whole-blood OAS1/MX1 induction without serum IFN-α, present vs present
engagement.population: Unselected (HBeAg-positive or -negative CHB, viremic or NA-suppressed)
engagement.judgement: Not a retrodiction: the monkey/mouse PK/PD is the IND-enabling work that set the presystemic concept before human dosing (Lanford 2013 already cites 'pre-systemic' trial doses); published after the human data, so medium confidence.
engagement.note: The same paper shows healthy volunteers, like monkeys, raised whole-blood OAS1 and MX1 after oral GS-9620 without systemic IFN-α.
engagement.short: Human ISGs presystemic, as in monkeys
engagement.quote: It is noteworthy that we also demonstrated that, in animals and healthy human volunteers, oral administration of GS-9620 can induce a type I interferon-dependent antiviral innate immune response, as measured by whole-blood mRNA of the ISGs
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the human data in the paper are presumably the Lopatin 2013 cohort (doi:10.3851/imp2548), which shows ISGs from 2 mg.
engagement.reason: Presystemic ISG induction seen in humans

dose.population: Unselected (HBeAg-positive or -negative CHB, viremic or NA-suppressed)
dose.note: The model defined a presystemic oral dose window: ISG induction below the doses that raise serum IFN-α.
dose.quote: It is noteworthy that we also demonstrated that, in animals and healthy human volunteers, oral administration of GS-9620 can induce a type I interferon-dependent antiviral innate immune response, as measured by whole-blood mRNA of the ISGs
dose.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: monkey and mouse oral PK/PD defining the presystemic window preceded the unregistered healthy-volunteer study (Lopatin 2013); paper epub 2013-10-16. Abstract-level reading (full text not retrieved).

dose.magnitude_basis: existence of an oral dose range with ISG induction but no serum IFN-α or AEs (humans 2-4 mg vs IFN-α at 8-12 mg)
dose.population: Unselected (HBeAg-positive or -negative CHB, viremic or NA-suppressed)
dose.judgement: Judgement call: read the model's presystemic window (ISGs without systemic IFN-α) as a stated regimen target plus a tolerability margin, not as mg/kg arithmetic. Humans were dosed to it without IFN-α toxicity, so same with margin_stated; whether it worked is efficacy, where this model made no antiviral prediction.
dose.note: Healthy volunteers induced ISGs from 2 mg, well below the doses giving serum IFN-α or adverse events: the presystemic window held.
dose.quote: Induction of chemokines/cytokines and IFN-stimulated genes were seen at GS-9620 doses ≥ 2 mg, well below doses that induced serum IFN-α or led to clinical adverse events.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Patients were later dosed inside the window (1-4 mg weekly) with mostly mild AEs (Gane 2015, Janssen 2018).

added_models.model: HBV-infected primary human hepatocytes and dHepaRG with GS-9620-treated PBMC conditioned media

efficacy.population: Unselected (HBeAg-positive or -negative CHB, viremic or NA-suppressed)
efficacy.note: Type I IFN from GS-9620-stimulated human PBMC durably reduced HBV DNA, RNA and antigens in infected human hepatocytes in vitro.
efficacy.quote: In contrast, GS-9620-CM induced prolonged reduction of HBV DNA, RNA, and antigen levels in PHH and dHepaRG cells via a type I interferon (IFN)-dependent mechanism.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HBsAg change: in vitro antigen reduction vs no HBsAg decline in NA-suppressed patients at week 24
efficacy.population: Unselected (HBeAg-positive or -negative CHB, viremic or NA-suppressed)
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the in vitro system was run after Gane 2015 had already reported no HBsAg change in patients, and it did not reproduce that (it showed antigen reduction), so contra. Low confidence: the conditioned media mimic systemic IFN-α that presystemic patient dosing never produced, and GS-9620 alone had no activity in PHH.
efficacy.note: Weekly vesatolimod did not lower HBsAg in patients, against the antigen reduction this in vitro system showed.
efficacy.quote: No significant declines in HBsAg were observed at the primary (Week 24) or secondary endpoints (Weeks 4, 8, 12, and 48).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers. Paired by me; registry date is NCT02166047 results posting.

patient_trials.quote: No clinically significant changes in HBsAg or HBV DNA levels were observed.
